Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National We do not fall under the Rent Act; hostel occupants are not tenants – UGEL Chief Officer Source : Albert Kuzor 18 November 2026 11:19am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Chief Executive Officer of the University of Ghana Enterprise Limited (UGEL), Yawo Agbesi, has argued that the university's hostel facilities do not fall under the Rent Act of the Rent Control Commission of the Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources because students who occupy them are not tenants.
He explained that UGEL does not enter into conventional landlord-tenant agreements with students, who instead apply for accommodation and leave the facilities after completing their studies.
According to him, the students are considered constituents of the university's accommodation system rather than tenants under a landlord-tenant arrangement.
"We are of the view that our students, or our constituents, as we call them, are not tenants and, among other things, we do not fall under the Rent Act, and it is subject to some level of interpretation," he said on JoyFM's Super Morning Show on Wednesday.
"We are not disputing the power and authority of the Rent Commissioner; he is doing a fantastic job, and we respect him for what he is doing, but we are of the view that, from the way we operate, we are not operating from a landlord-tenant relationship," he added.
Mr Agbesi emphasised that "They [students] come in, they pay for a short period, they leave, and then the next semester they apply."
Mr Agbesi's comments follow a confrontation between Acting Rent Commissioner Frederick Opoku and a hostel manager during an inspection of UGEL-operated facilities on the University of Ghana campus.

The incident, which was captured in a viral video, has triggered debate over the authority of the Rent Control Department to inspect the university's hostels.
Mr Opoku has disclosed that UGEL, through its lawyers, wrote to him asking him not to visit the facilities.
UGEL says it is preparing to file a court action to seek interpretation of the Rent Act in relation to hostels.
